review.summary: The patch reworks ForwardDiff's NaN-safe partial arithmetic in src/partials.jl from a whole-tuple guard to a per-element guard. Previously the NaN-safe guards (`ifelse(!isfinite(x) && iszero(partials), one(x), x)`) only kicked in when every partial in the tuple was zero, so a Partials object mixing zero and non-zero components still produced NaN in the zero slots when scaled by a non-finite factor or divided by zero. The new `_mul_partial`/`_div_partial` helpers apply the zero-partial short circuit component-wise inside `scale_tuple`, `div_tuple_by_scalar`, and `mul_tuples`, which is the documented intent of NANSAFE_MODE. This is a behavioral correctness fix in production code, not an API addition: the new helpers are internal, and the `*`, `/`, `_mul_partials` methods are just hoisted out of the mode-conditional branch unchanged in the non-NaN-safe path.
review.evidence: Single production file (src/partials.jl), 4 hunks, all reported necessary and globally minimal. Test changes accompany the fix across test/PartialsTest.jl, test/DerivativeTest.jl, and test/GradientTest.jl, indicating observable behavior differences at both the Partials level and the derivative/gradient level. Runtime evidence reports a stable differential over 3 repetitions via a dedicated trigger script, with the full suite passing at the fixed commit. The semantics of the diff independently support a defect: the old guard's `iszero(partials)` condition is strictly weaker than the per-element `iszero(partial)` condition, so mixed zero/non-zero partial tuples were not protected.

review.validation_risks: The fix only changes user-visible behavior when NANSAFE_MODE_ENABLED is true, which is a compile-time preference in ForwardDiff; if the harness runs with the default (disabled) setting, the trigger test may not reproduce. Note also that `mul_tuples` changes multiplication operand order from `afactor * a[i]` to `_mul_partial(a[i], afactor)`, which is semantically identical for real floats but could shift results for non-commutative or promotion-sensitive element types, so a differential failure might come from that rather than the NaN guard. Tests asserting NaN outputs are sensitive to signed zero and NaN equality semantics, so use isnan/iszero rather than == comparisons.
review.suggested_tests: 1) Construct a Partials with mixed components, e.g. Partials((0.0, 1.0)), and check that multiplying by Inf and dividing by 0.0 yields 0.0 in the zero slot instead of NaN under NaN-safe mode. 2) Exercise `_mul_partials(a, b, x_a, x_b)` where only one of a or b has a zero component and one factor is non-finite, asserting the zero component stays zero. 3) End-to-end: differentiate a function whose primal hits a non-finite intermediate for one seeded direction only (the DerivativeTest/GradientTest additions likely cover this) and assert no NaN appears in the gradient entries corresponding to zero partials. 4) Regression guard: verify the non-NaN-safe path results are numerically unchanged for a representative set of Partials operations.
